binders: There exists one real constant C, chosen before all other objects.
Universally quantify over every type Omega with a measurable-space structure, every probability measure mu on Omega, and every function X : Omega -> Real.

For the all-pairs clause, universally quantify over indices i and j among the four cases of LocalDef003 and over a real input scale Ki; the output scale Kj is existential and may depend on Omega, mu, X, i, j, and Ki.

For the centered comparisons, universally quantify over a positive input scale K2 or K5; each existential output scale may depend on the ambient probability space, X, and its corresponding input scale.
hypotheses: The ambient measure mu is a probability measure.
Each conversion assumes its input scale is strictly positive and that X satisfies the indicated predicate with that input scale.
The two comparisons between the moment predicate and LocalDef001 are required only under the outer assumption that X is integrable and integral X dmu = 0.
conclusions: For every ordered pair i,j of the four indexed predicates and every positive Ki for which the i-predicate holds, there exists Kj > 0 with Kj <= C Ki for which the j-predicate holds.
If X is integrable and centered, then any positive K2 satisfying the LocalDef004-indexed moment predicate yields a positive K5 <= C K2 satisfying LocalDef001.
If X is integrable and centered, then any positive K5 satisfying LocalDef001 yields a positive K2 <= C K5 satisfying the LocalDef004-indexed moment predicate.
mathematical_definitions: Write T_K(X) for: X is measurable, K > 0, and for every t >= 0, mu{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t/K). This is the LocalDef011 case of LocalDef002.

Write M_K(X) for: X is measurable, K > 0, X is almost-everywhere measurable, and for every real p >= 1, |X|^p is integrable and integral |X|^p dmu <= (K p)^p, using real powers. This is the LocalDef004 case.

Write A_K(X) for: X is measurable, K > 0, and for every real lambda with 0 <= lambda <= 1/K, exp(lambda |X|) is integrable and integral exp(lambda |X|) dmu <= exp(K lambda). This is the LocalDef009 case.
Write O_K(X) for: X is measurable, K > 0, exp(|X|/K) is integrable, and integral exp(|X|/K) dmu <= 2. This is the LocalDef010 case.

Write G_K(X) for: X is measurable, K > 0, X is integrable with integral X dmu = 0, and for every real lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K, exp(lambda X) is integrable and integral exp(lambda X) dmu <= exp(K^2 lambda^2). This is LocalDef001.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal real constant C >= 1 such that, on every probability space and for every real-valued function X, each of the four explicitly defined conditions T, M, A, and O at a positive scale implies each of the other three (and itself) at some positive scale no larger than C times the original scale. Moreover, whenever X is integrable and has mean zero, the moment condition M and the centered local MGF condition G imply one another up to the same multiplicative constant C on their scale parameters: M at K2 gives G at some K5 <= C K2, and G at K5 gives M at some K2 <= C K5.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The same single constant C must work uniformly for every measurable space, probability measure, real-valued X, ordered pair of the four indices, and both centered conversion directions.
All input and witness scales are required to be strictly positive. The local predicates themselves also include positivity, so some positivity premises are redundant but explicit.

Every indexed predicate requires actual measurability of X, not merely almost-everywhere measurability. The moment predicate additionally contains AEMeasurable X, which is redundant once Measurable X holds.
The moment exponent p ranges over all real p >= 1 and uses Real.rpow; it is not restricted to integers.

The absolute-value MGF condition is only for 0 <= lambda <= 1/K and has the exact bound exp(K lambda). The centered MGF condition is only for |lambda| <= 1/K and has the exact bound exp(K^2 lambda^2); neither condition asserts an all-lambda MGF estimate.

The centered moment-to-MGF and MGF-to-moment conclusions sit under an outer implication from integrability and zero mean. If that outer antecedent fails, both conclusions hold vacuously. LocalDef001 independently includes integrability and zero mean, making those outer assumptions redundant for the LocalDef001-to-moment direction.

Every individual conversion is an implication and is vacuous if its indexed input predicate has no positive scale for the chosen X. The theorem does not assert that any of the four predicates holds for every X.
The theorem compares admissible scale parameters by existence of a possibly different output scale; it does not define optimal constants, infima, norms, or equality of best scales.
Tail probabilities use Measure.real, i.e. ENNReal.toReal applied to the measure of the event. Under the probability-measure assumption these values are finite, so this does not lose infinite mass.

The theorem encodes no independence assumptions, no product or sum of random variables, no almost-sure identification convention for X, and no claim about any objects beyond the displayed one-variable predicates.
